claims: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign currently has no official mascot.
The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign athletic teams are known as the Fighting Illini.
The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign retired Chief Illiniwek in 2007.
The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign has not had an official mascot since 2007.
The King's Guard is a student-led group.
The King's Guard is actively pushing for the Belted Kingfisher as a new unofficial mascot.
The Belted Kingfisher is often dubbed the "Kingfisher".
The Belted Kingfisher is being proposed to represent the Fighting Illini.
The Belted Kingfisher mascot is depicted as a bird with blue and orange feathers.
The blue and orange feathers match the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign’s colors.
The Kingfisher is not yet the official University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign mascot.
The Kingfisher has appeared at games and campus events in a costume.
The Kingfisher received positive student reactions.
The King's Guard initiative gained momentum after a 2020 student referendum.
A 2020 student referendum favored the Kingfisher.
Chief Illiniwek was a Native American-styled mascot.
Chief Illiniwek was used from the 1970s until 2007.
The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign retired Chief Illiniwek after the NCAA labeled it "hostile and abusive".
